2. Primary functional requirements — use cases

UC-1 — Record a transaction

  • Primary actor: Registered user
  • Supporting actors: —
  • Trigger: User submits the "add transaction" form
  • Preconditions: User is authenticated
  • Main success scenario: 1. User enters amount, date, category, note. 2. System validates. 3. System persists the transaction. 4. System updates the dashboard aggregates. 5. System confirms.
  • Key alternate / exception flows: 2a. Validation fails → field-level errors, no write. 3a. Store unavailable → queued write, user told "saved, syncing".
  • Architectural significance: dominates write load; on the p95 latency path (PQA-1); touched by every modifiability change (MQA-1).
  • Related drivers: BG-1, PQA-1, MQA-1

UC-2 — View the monthly dashboard

  • Primary actor: Registered user
  • Supporting actors: —
  • Trigger: User opens the app or navigates to "Dashboard"
  • Preconditions: User is authenticated; has ≥ 0 transactions
  • Main success scenario: 1. System loads the user's month-to-date aggregates. 2. System renders totals, a category breakdown chart, recent transactions, and savings-goal progress.
  • Key alternate / exception flows: 1a. Aggregates cache miss → recompute from the transaction store.
  • Architectural significance: the performance-critical read path (PQA-1); shapes the read-model / caching decision.
  • Related drivers: BG-1, PQA-1, UQA-1

UC-3 — Import a bank statement (CSV)

  • Primary actor: Registered user
  • Supporting actors: —
  • Trigger: User uploads a CSV file
  • Preconditions: User is authenticated
  • Main success scenario: 1. User uploads CSV. 2. System parses and maps rows to transactions. 3. System asks the user to confirm category mapping. 4. System bulk-inserts. 5. System updates aggregates.
  • Key alternate / exception flows: 2a. Unrecognised format → guided column mapping. 4a. Partial failure → per-row result report.
  • Architectural significance: bulk write path; <<include>>s categorisation; first candidate for async processing.
  • Related drivers: BG-1, PQA-2

6. Prioritised driver list (input to ADD / ATAM)

  1. SQA-1 (H,H) — reject and log cross-user access; 0 successful reads
  2. AQA-1 (H,H) — 99.5 % monthly uptime; AZ failure recovers < 60 s
  3. PQA-1 (H,M) — dashboard interactive < 1.5 s @ p95 at 500 concurrent users
  4. UC-1 — record a transaction (write-load + latency + modifiability hot spot)
  5. UC-2 — monthly dashboard (performance-critical read path)
  6. CON-4 (hard) — encryption in transit and at rest
  7. CON-2 (hard) — one engineer, 3-month MVP

Architecture: Personal Finance Tracker

1. Introduction

A mobile-web personal finance tracker. This document is the ADD 3.0 working architecture after iteration 1 (overall structure, security, availability) and iteration 2 (dashboard read path). Drivers: ../drivers.md.

2. Context diagram

Diagram

Description

A single external dependency at launch: a transactional email provider. Everything else is owned by the system, keeping the SOC 2 (CON-4) surface small.

4. Container diagram

Diagram

Description

The API service is the single write path and the single place tenant scoping (SQA-1) is enforced. The Redis read cache serves the dashboard (PQA-1); it is a performance element, not a system of record, so its loss degrades latency but not correctness (AQA-1).

5. Component diagrams

API Service

Diagram

Description

Every request passes through the Tenant Guard before any service runs, so cross-tenant access (SQA-1) is structurally prevented rather than checked per-endpoint.

6. Sequence diagrams

On a cache hit the database is not touched, which is the common path and keeps p95 under the 1.5 s budget (PQA-1). On a miss the API recomputes from tenant-scoped rows and repopulates the cache; a stale cache is bounded by the 15-minute TTL.

7. Deployment diagram

Diagram

Description

The API runs as stateless replicas spread across two AZs behind the platform load balancer, and the data tier uses managed primary/standby with automated failover — together these meet AQA-1 (single-AZ failure recovers < 60 s) within the CON-3 low-cost-tier constraint.

9. Design decisions

DecisionRationale (cite driver IDs)Alternatives discarded
Single API service owns all writes and enforces tenant scoping in one middlewareSQA-1 needs one auditable choke point; CON-2 favours few moving partsPer-service authz checks (easy to miss one)
Redis cache-aside for dashboard aggregates with 15-min TTLPQA-1 p95 budget; DB alone won't meet it at 500 concurrentMaterialised views (slower to iterate — MQA-1); CDN caching (per-user data)
Managed PostgreSQL primary/standby, multi-AZ, automated failoverAQA-1 recovery target; CON-5 mandates PostgreSQL; CON-3 low-cost tier still offers thisSelf-managed HA (CON-2 time), single instance (fails AQA-1)
